clue.text: Conceited American in Bordeaux?

indicators.note: 'in' puts one piece bodily inside another instead of alongside it

parts.note: a Bordeaux is a wine, and wine in the town it comes from is vin
A is the dictionary abbreviation for America or American

explanation.walkthrough: Bordeaux does two jobs at once: it names the drink and it sets the language you name it in. The question mark is the setter apologising for the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain means full of your own looks or worth, the conceited sense rather than the 'in vain' one meaning fruitless.

clue.text: Fifth and final poet returning to visit fine eastern city

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five, so it stands for fifth

indicators.note: the reversed poet visits the final word, going inside it

parts.note: last means final

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the poet's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A fifth and last trip by a poet coming back to see a fine city in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: OVID reversed is DIVO, which goes inside LAST after LA, between V and OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladivostok is the major Russian port city on the Pacific, in the far east of the country.

clue.text: Asian runner visiting Germany and America

parts.note: someone visiting is in, the way a doctor is in
D is Germany's international car plate, for Deutschland
US is the everyday short form of the country

explanation.walkthrough: No indicator anywhere: three pieces simply run on in clue order, which is the shape to look for when every word is a country or a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus runs from Tibet down through Pakistan, so 'runner' names it by what a river does and 'Asian' says which one.

clue.text: Douglas here maintains svelte physique eating zero fat meals primarily

indicators.note: the lean phrase eats the other letters, taking them inside

parts.note: someone who keeps a svelte physique is lean, read as the two words is lean
O looks like zero

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letters of the words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of fat and meals are F and M

explanation.surface: A man called Douglas stays slim by cutting fat from his meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Douglas' looks like a person, but it is the island's capital. IS LEAN eats O, F and M between its LE and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the capital town of the Isle of Man, the British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Discuss idle site to be repurposed after decentralisation, and related matters

indicators.note: letters put to a new purpose are the same letters doing a different job, which means a different order
take the centre out of each word — the middle letter of an odd one, the middle pair of an even one

parts.note: DISCUSS has seven letters, so its centre is the C, and out it comes
IDLE has an even middle, DL, and both letters go
SITE loses its middle pair IT the same way

explanation.walkthrough: Three words are hollowed out before anything is shuffled, which is why counting the clue's letters never reaches ten. The planning-committee surface hides both steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Side issues are the questions that come up alongside the main one — connected, but off to one side of what is actually being decided.

clue.text: Ireland's old monarch trending

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, and 'old' marks her as the reign before this one
what is trending is in — in fashion, in vogue

explanation.walkthrough: ER is a crossword workhorse, and since the accession it needs flagging as the previous monarch: that is the job 'old' is doing, not describing an ancient king.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland, from the Irish Eirinn, the word behind the toast 'Erin go bragh'.

clue.text: Consequences of following a large thug

parts.note: f. is the footnote abbreviation for following
the article is taken at face value as its own letter
L is the clothing label for large
a lout is a thug in four letters

explanation.walkthrough: Three single letters in a row is a shape worth recognising: 'a large' adds nothing to the picture of a thug, and words that pull no weight in the surface are usually initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallout is the dust that settles after an explosion, so 'Consequences' takes the word figuratively — the mess left once something has gone off.

clue.text: Film in musical venue

parts.note: Annie, the red-haired orphan, is the musical
a hall is where a concert is put on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical venue' reads as one phrase, a place gigs happen, and is really two separate clues laid end to end. There is no indicator at all to warn you.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie Hall is Woody Allen's 1977 romantic comedy, so 'Film' defines it by category — the answer is a title, not a description.

clue.text: Bonus promotion almost over

parts.note: an ad is a promotion, an advertisement

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: done means over, finished

explanation.surface: An advertising offer for extras that has nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE without its final E is DON, after AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra feature or item supplied in addition, a bonus.

clue.text: King abandons Lancelot for one dark period

indicators.note: to abandon something is to walk off and leave it behind you, so that letter is simply gone

parts.note: Lancelot is one of the Round Table's knights, and 'for one' marks him as an example
K is the king on a chessboard and in a pack of cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like part of the Arthurian scenery and is really an abbreviation. Deciding which words of a surface are letters is most of the work in a clue like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark stretch between sunset and sunrise, so 'dark period' defines it by the one property that separates it from day.

clue.text: Practising dental work?

definitions.meaning: troops rehearsing formations, or pupils repeating exercises, are both practising through repetition
the drill boring into a tooth is the dentist's own verb

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are -ing words, which is what makes the seam invisible: the clue reads as one activity, a dentist rehearsing, and is really two definitions side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers and pupils drilling are practising by repetition, while a dentist drilling is boring into a tooth: one word, two unconnected trades.

clue.text: Endless, asinine rubbish about Instagram symbol

indicators.note: endless means the end is missing, so the word beside it gives up its final letter
a piece placed about another wraps round it, sitting on both sides
rubbish is what has been thrown out and jumbled together, and letters treated that way lose their order

parts.note: asinine hands over everything but its last letter
IG is how Instagram is written in a handle or a hashtag

explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Endless' is the disguise. It makes the word look like a second adjective describing rubbish, when its job is to dock a letter off the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An insignia is the badge or emblem that marks rank or membership, so 'symbol' names it by the job it does.

clue.text: Very fast body of water

parts.note: 'so tired' and 'very tired' are the same intensifier
Lent is the church's forty-day fast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is the noun here, a stretch of going without food, not the adverb. 'Very' sitting in front of it is what pushes you towards speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Solent is the strait between Hampshire and the Isle of Wight, so 'body of water' names it by category rather than describing it.

clue.text: Pyramid model done rather crudely

indicators.note: work done crudely is thrown together with no care for where anything lands, which is what happens to these letters

parts.note: the Model T Ford is the crossword's standard model
ten letters taken exactly as they stand, to be shaken up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather' is fodder rather than an adverb softening 'crudely', and that is the hard part: the sentence reads as plain English right up to the point you count the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron has four triangular faces, which is what a pyramid becomes once its base is a triangle instead of a square.

clue.text: Rally and unite to secure new victory

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within your grasp, which is where these letters end up

parts.note: to coalesce is to come together into one
N is the standard abbreviation for new
V is victory, as in the V-sign and VE Day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' is the medical sense, a patient rallying, which is why it can sit next to 'unite' without either word looking more like the definition than the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To convalesce is to regain strength after illness, and a patient who rallies is doing exactly that — winning ground back.

clue.text: Old bishop behind society for religious people

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old, as in OAP
B is the bishop in chess notation
a train running behind is running late
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.walkthrough: Three of the four pieces are single letters, and the one that is not hides behind a word you would naturally read as a position. Hunt the abbreviations first.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblates are lay people who have offered themselves to a monastery's service, so 'religious people' names them by that dedication rather than by any order.

clue.text: Western actor playing evil men, including a Republican

indicators.note: an actor playing a part is not himself, and letters playing at being a word are not in their own order
what is included sits inside, so this pair goes within the shuffled letters rather than after them

parts.note: seven letters offered up to be rearranged
the article taken as its own letter
R is the ballot-paper abbreviation for a Republican

explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing evil men' is a straight description of the man's career, which is exactly why it reads as biography instead of as an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Marvin starred in westerns from The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance to Cat Ballou, so 'Western actor' names him by the genre he owned.

clue.text: Have more staying power than half-hearted social reject

indicators.note: the heart of the word is the Roman numeral for a hundred, and halving it gives the numeral for fifty

parts.note: an outcast is someone rejected by society

explanation.surface: A feeble attempt to outlast a social pariah.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of OUTCAST is C, the Roman numeral 100; halved it becomes L, 50.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlast someone is to keep going longer than they do, having more stamina.

clue.text: In secondary education? Rest and eat before start of exam

indicators.note: 'before' is placing rather than timing: the pieces already named sit in front of the letter that follows

parts.note: a golf ball rests on a tee, so a tee is a rest
a worry that eats at you nags at you

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, and that single letter is all this asks for

parts.note: the opening letter of Exam

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest and eat' sounds like advice for the night before a paper, which is the scene the surface wants. Both words are really nouns and verbs to be swapped for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage covers thirteen to nineteen, roughly the years a pupil spends at secondary school, and the question mark admits the fit is by example.

clue.text: Language master's superseding bachelor's in another language

indicators.note: superseding means taking the place of, so the master's letters replace the bachelor's

parts.note: Arabic is a language, distinct from the one defined
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree
MA is a master's degree, Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A graduate's master's degree replaces their bachelor's, gained in a foreign language.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about degrees: a master's superseding a bachelor's. In ARABIC the B (bachelor) gives way to MA (master).
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue of the Near East, the vernacular spoken in Jesus's time, so it is a language.

clue.text: Pedestrian unlucky to meet a vehicle coming first

indicators.note: whatever comes first goes at the front, ahead of everything the clue has already handed you

parts.note: a van is the vehicle, and it leads despite being named last
ill luck is bad luck, so unlucky is ill
the article taken at face value

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' is the adjective meaning dull, but the road-accident surface keeps it looking like a person on foot right up until the letters are in.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla has come to mean plain and unadorned — vanilla software, vanilla sex — which is the dull sense 'pedestrian' carries.

clue.text: Nine gross only?

parts.note: 'only' rules out everything else, and what it rules out here is the other figure
a sum is quoted gross or net, so naming one denies the other

explanation.walkthrough: Nine gross would be 1,296 if the arithmetic were meant seriously. The question mark is there because the answer is a group of nine rather than the number itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is nine musicians, or the piece written for them, so 'Nine' names the group the way 'eleven' names a football side.

clue.text: End of combat that's unfortunate for indigenous Australians

parts.note: a knockout ends a fight, and KO is how it is written
alas is what you say when something is unfortunate

explanation.walkthrough: 'End of combat' looks like an instruction to take one last letter, and 'indigenous Australians' points hard at people. Both readings are the setter's, and neither is the one you want.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas live wild only in eastern Australia, so 'indigenous Australians' is literally true of them — native, and found nowhere else on earth.

clue.text: Make extended remix of metal song principally lacking energy

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, so the letters are put in a new order
the principal, first, letters of metal and song are missing

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A producer stretches out a heavy-metal track in a new mix, though it lacks punch.
explanation.walkthrough: METAL SONG without M and S leaves ETALONG; add E and rearrange. 'lacking energy' looks like one phrase, but energy is an extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate something is to make it longer, to extend it.

clue.text: Revolving set about to cause problems

indicators.note: a thing revolving turns right round, so the letters assembled here are read back the other way

parts.note: to set something down is to put it down
ca. is short for circa, the 'about' in front of a date

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set about' reads as one phrasal verb, starting on a job, and is really two separate pieces. Splitting it is what makes the turn possible to see.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or malfunction — a child or a gearbox acting up — which is causing trouble rather than doing anything deliberate.

clue.text: Anonymous person taking small quantity of medication

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside you, so this letter goes within the other piece

parts.note: John Doe is the name given to a man nobody can name
S is the size label for small

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is one sentence about a patient with pills, and the split falls between 'small' and 'quantity' — an awkward place, which is why the definition is hard to find.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose is the measured amount of a drug you take at one time, so 'quantity of medication' is that definition written out longhand.

clue.text: Pilots' map readers ignoring leader — not good

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its head, and ignoring it means beginning at the second
'not' cancels whatever follows it, so the letter that word stands for is taken away

parts.note: the ones who read the maps are the navigators
the letter leading NAVIGATORS is its N
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.walkthrough: The dash does a lot of quiet work: it makes 'not good' read as a judgement on the map readers rather than as a second instruction to drop a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is one who flies an aircraft, the older and grander word for the job, so 'Pilots' is the everyday plural synonym.

clue.text: Express disapproval over royal governess?

parts.note: tut is the noise you make to show disapproval
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
R is Rex or Regina, the royal signature

explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is not doing anything directional here — it is the cricketing abbreviation, which is why the three pieces simply run on in the order the clue gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: A governess is a private tutor living with the family, so the question mark admits the definition names one kind of tutor rather than all of them.

clue.text: I'm not sure journalist's stalking ability is exhausted

indicators.note: to stalk someone is to follow at their back, so these pieces settle behind the piece they are stalking

parts.note: a knack is the ability to do something easily
er is the noise of someone who is not sure
the journalist is the editor, ED

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ability is exhausted' reads as one idea, a talent run dry, and that is what stops you cutting the clue at its last word, where the definition actually starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Knackered is British slang for worn out, from the knacker's yard where spent horses ended up, so 'exhausted' is the same idea in polite register.

clue.text: Familiar with riding?

definitions.note: 'Riding' is a verb and UPON a preposition, so the two do not swap cleanly: the question mark covers the stretch, since you ride by sitting upon the animal.
definitions.meaning: someone well versed in a subject is often said to be on top of it, right up to speed
a rider sits astride the horse, literally on top of it

explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration says one word and the first definition wants two, up on. Those four letters read either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Up on the news means familiar with it, while a rider sits upon a horse: the same four letters, spaced in one sense and closed in the other.
